provisions.title: New Jersey Data Privacy Act: controller duties (consent for sensitive data; no sale of sensitive data)
provisions.quote: not process sensitive data concerning a consumer without first obtaining the consumer's consent
provisions.appliesTo: Controllers that "control or process the personal data of at least 100,000 consumers, excluding personal data processed solely for the purpose of completing a payment transaction" (N.J.S.A. 56:8-166.5, P.L.2023, c.266, s.2), or 25,000 consumers plus revenue from sale. The sale ban applies "regardless of the number of consumers".

provisions.title: New Jersey Data Privacy Act: definition of sensitive data
provisions.quote: "Sensitive data" means personal data revealing racial or ethnic origin; religious beliefs; mental or physical health condition, treatment, or diagnosis
provisions.appliesTo: Definition used by P.L.2023, c.266 (C.56:8-166.4 et seq.).

provisions.title: Data brokers and data collectors: ban on sale of sensitive data
provisions.quote: In no case shall a data broker or data collector sell or license sensitive data to any other individual or entity.
provisions.appliesTo: Data brokers and data collectors; excludes protected health information held by a HIPAA covered entity or business associate.

consumer_health_data.note: The New Jersey Data Privacy Act requires opt-in consent to process sensitive data, which includes health data. Since 30 June 2026 sale of sensitive data is banned. It is a comprehensive law, not a dedicated consumer health data law.

crossCheck.note: Quotes, citations and dates hold. P.L.2026, c.25 approved 30 June 2026, effective immediately. P.L.2025, c.367 approved 20 January 2026, effective immediately. Opt-in consent for sensitive data gives level 2. No dedicated consumer health data law found.

facts.statutoryDamages: None fixed. Genetic Privacy Act: all actual damages. HIV records: actual damages, equitable relief, attorney's fees, punitive damages for wanton or malicious conduct; each disclosure a separate offense.

provisions.title: Genetic Privacy Act: civil liability for unlawful disclosure
provisions.quote: Any person who discloses an individual's genetic information in violation of P.L.1996, c.126, shall be liable to the individual for all actual damages, including damages for economic, bodily, or emotional harm which is proximately caused by the disclosure.
provisions.appliesTo: Any person who discloses genetic information in violation of the act.

provisions.title: AIDS and HIV records: civil actions against violators
provisions.quote: A person who has or is suspected of having AIDS or HIV infection who is aggrieved as a result of a violation of this act may commence a civil action against the individual or institution who committed the violation to obtain appropriate relief
provisions.appliesTo: Individuals or institutions violating the AIDS and HIV records provisions.

provisions.title: New Jersey Data Privacy Act: Attorney General enforcement only
provisions.quote: shall be construed as providing the basis for, or subject to, a private right of action for violations of P.L.2023, c.266

private_right.note: Private suits exist for two narrow record categories: genetic information and HIV records. The Data Privacy Act has no private right. Willful breach-law violations are Consumer Fraud Act violations (N.J.S.A. 56:8-166), which allows suits for ascertainable loss.

crossCheck.note: Private suits exist for genetic and HIV records only, which fits level 1. Data Privacy Act took effect 15 January 2025, the 365th day after 16 January 2024 approval, with no private right.
